predecessors.name: Rhodes
predecessors.text: Lycia, 'awarded to Rhodes in the Peace of Apamea in 188 BC' and taken back by Rome in 168 BC

successors.name: Roman Empire
successors.text: Lycia, annexed by Claudius in 43 AD; joined with Pamphylia as Lycia et Pamphylia by Vespasian in 74

ledger.x: 168: Rome frees Lycia from Rhodes and the Lycian League stands as a protectorate.
168: Lycia is a protectorate of Rome.
42: Brutus comes to Lycia for money before Philippi and besieges Xanthos after the League refused to contribute.
27 BC: the Roman side of the protectorate passes from the Republic to the Principate.
27 BC: Lycia is a free ally of the Roman Empire under Augustus.
43: the Lycian League ends as an independent state.

wars.name: Brutus's Lycian campaign
wars.outcome: Brutus came to Lycia 'to obtain funds before the Battle of Philippi' and 'besieged Xanthos after the Lycian League refused to contribute'; the page gives the city 'rebuilt under Mark Antony' without a year.

wars.name: Lycian revolt and the annexation of Lycia
wars.outcome: Claudius annexed Lycia in 43 AD; Cassius Dio, quoted on the Lycian League page, says he 'reduced the Lycians to servitude because they had revolted'.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier for the League; Lycia is drawn as the Teke Peninsula region.
